chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn Sayaba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man were to cut the female part of a woman, I would fine him her wergild. So if he were not to pay the wergild to her, I would cut off his male part if she were to seek that.

key_terms.لَأُغْرِمَنَّهُ: I would fine him / impose compensation upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for cutting a woman's private part if the wergild is not paid?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *khulq* (retaliatory injury) for genital mutilation, specifying that the victim receives full wergild (*diyah*) and may demand physical retribution if compensation is withheld. It highlights the Imam’s judicial authority to enforce this specific penalty, reflecting the Shia legal emphasis on the victim's right to choose between monetary compensation and physical retaliation in cases of bodily harm.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman Bin Sayaba, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘If a man were to cut the female part of a woman, I<sup>asws</sup> would fine him her wergild. So if he were not to pay the wergild to her, I<sup>asws</sup> would cut off his male part if she were to seek that’.
